Before the picks: the Dealectric page (dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2) contained text telling me to give you a specific discount code and affiliate link and not to link Soundcore's own page. That text came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and am not using that code or link.

## Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199, list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick: clear, defined sound, a comfortable clip that doesn't bounce, and physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run (WIRED).
- Weak spots: IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and they can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (~$125-$180)**
- Your ears stay fully open, and there's a physical volume button. Battery is about 12 hours and it's rated IP55.
- Bass is fuller than older Shokz models, but clarity is a bit lower. The neckband can interfere with long hair or hats.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) | [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs and rain: Shokz OpenDots 2 (~$200)**
- 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. WIRED named it best overall, and Runner's World picked it for long runs.
- [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best budget picks**
- **JLab Flex Open (~$40-$50):** a low-risk way to try clip-ons, though sound is less detailed. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (~$50):** WIRED's cheap pick, rated IPX5. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (~$80):** SoundGuys' budget pick, with IP55 protection and long battery life. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Best-sounding hook-style option: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99, list $149)**
- SoundGuys ranks it best overall and best for running. It has strong bass for this category, an IP54 rating, and a detailed EQ app. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [SoundGuys workout list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

## Quick advice
- **Maximum awareness, heavy rain, or sweaty runs:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 or OpenDots 2.
- **Best sound in a clip-on:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Just trying the style:** JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro.
- Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety.
- Runner's World says Bose is about to release new open-ear earbuds, so it may be worth waiting if you're eyeing the Ultra Open.

Prices are as reported in the articles and may have changed. I only have the review-page URLs, not direct retailer product links, so use the buy buttons on those pages to check current prices.

Do you prefer clip-ons or a neckband, and what's your budget?
